old_behaviour: SET table silently removes exact duplicate rows. Seeded staging has 300 rows, 250 distinct; source has 250. runner.py enforces UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
new_behaviour: Plain Snowflake table keeps all 300 rows. No DISTINCT or owner-approved SET decision has been added.
question: Should exact duplicate storage usage be discarded or retained for charging? Choose distinct or keep_all explicitly; warehouse/dbt/macros/set_table_semantics.sql already requires that decision.

old_behaviour: ROW_NUMBER partitions by DOCUMENT_ID and sorts only VERSION_TS DESC. Fifty seeded documents have two distinct versions at the same latest timestamp; winner is unspecified.
new_behaviour: Candidate keeps the same incomplete ordering. A local matching winner does not establish deterministic parity across engines.
question: Which version wins equal latest timestamps? No VERSION_NO/ID tie breaker will be invented.

old_behaviour: XML lookup policy is Use First Value. For multiple role grants per USER_ID the runner selects the first cached match.
new_behaviour: Existing pc_content__doc_share joins every matching role. The local merge guard rejects duplicate SHARE_IDs instead of choosing a role. Seeded 20-row ROLE_GRANT has unique USER_IDs, so this is a synthetic error-case difference, not an observed seeded mismatch.
question: Which role wins for users with multiple grants? Preserve first cached match or choose an explicit role precedence? Existing dbt model is unchanged.

old_behaviour: Actual legacy job writes lake/audit/security_alert_anomaly and also overwrites JDBC sfx_audit.SPARK_ALERT_ANOMALY through common.runtime.save. Its manifest subject is documents although its input and both outputs are audit.
new_behaviour: Manifest-target dbt model computes the lake rowset in MART_SPARK but does not publish a JDBC table or an approved COMPAT replacement. That additional relation is declared but unavailable, not inferred from lake parity.
question: Who owns the audit JDBC publication, and should its callers move to the manifest Snowflake model or require an explicit compatibility publisher?

old_behaviour: main calls drop_unpartitioned then save_partition for one run_date. Cleanup retains older run_date= directories; nonempty writes dynamically overwrite only the current partition. Existing historical partitions therefore survive.
new_behaviour: The manifest-target table model and local proof compute the selected current run_date only. A table rebuild would replace history, not preserve older partitions. Actual fixture has one run_date and matches 200/200; multi-date retention is not established by that result.
question: Preserve all historical run_date snapshots, or approve a current-snapshot-only target? No retention policy or incremental materialization has been guessed.
